#Changes Since Deliverable 3
 
* **Updated Data Dictionary & Cleanliness:** Refined variable descriptions and verified missing values.
 * **Added Exploratory Data Visualizations:** Implemented four distinct ggplot2 charts.
```{r create-data}
spotify_us_songs <- read.csv("spotify_us_songs.csv")
spotify_df <- spotify_us_songs

```

### 1. The Distribution of One Variable (Histogram)
```{r viz-histogram}
spotify_df <- spotify_us_songs
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)



# Calculate average popularity per artist and get the top 25
top_artists <- spotify_df %>%
  group_by(artists) %>%
  summarise(avg_popularity = mean(popularity, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_popularity)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 25)

# Create the horizontal bar plot
ggplot(top_artists, aes(x = avg_popularity, y = reorder(artists, avg_popularity))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1DB954") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 25 Artists by Average Popularity",
    x = "Average Popularity Score",
    y = "Artist"
  )
```


num_rows <- nrow(spotify_df)
num_cols <- ncol(spotify_df)

# Check for null or NA cells per column
colSums(is.na(spotify_df))

# Correlation matrix of numeric audio attributes
numeric_spotify <- spotify_df %>% select(where(is.numeric))
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_spotify, use = "complete.obs")
print(round(cor_matrix, 2))

---
### 2. A Comparison Across Groups (Box Plot)
```{r viz-boxplot}
spotify_df <- spotify_us_songs

ggplot(spotify_df, aes(x = energy, y = danceability)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "#1DB954") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Danceability vs. Energy",
    x = "Energy Score",
    y = "Danceability Score"
  )
```
```{r viz-scatterplot}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

spotify_df <- spotify_us_songs

# Get the top 25 songs by popularity
top_songs <- spotify_df %>%
  arrange(desc(popularity)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)

# Create a horizontal bar chart
ggplot(top_songs, aes(x = popularity, y = reorder(name, popularity))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1DB954") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 30 Songs\nby by Popularity",
    x = "Popularity Score",
    y = "Song Name"
  )
```
```{r viz-scatterplot-2}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

spotify_df <- spotify_us_songs

# Get the top 25 songs with the highest positive weekly movement
top_weekly <- spotify_df %>%
  arrange(desc(weekly_movement)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 25) %>%
  mutate(short_name = str_trunc(name, 30))

# Create a horizontal bar chart
ggplot(top_weekly, aes(x = weekly_movement, y = reorder(short_name, weekly_movement))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1DB954") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 25 Songs by Weekly Movement",
    x = "Weekly Movement (Positions Gained)",
    y = "Song Name"
  )

```


## 5. Discussion
Through the exploratory data analysis of the Spotify dataset, I learned how crucial clean variable structuring and consistent aesthetic palettes (ggplot2) are for communicating insights clearly. I was surprised by how cleanly the linear relationship between energy and danceability appeared even in a small sample.
Moving forward into the draft stage, open questions remain regarding whether these audio features stay consistent across different markets or time periods. To prepare my final project draft, I plan to expand the dataset sample size, run correlation tests, and model which attributes most reliably predict track success
